text:
GitHub Copilot can use your browser. Give it a test, not a tour.

Browser use entered public preview November 17: Copilot can interact with web apps and help test them.

On Tech Thursday, our Copilot CLI image batch ran, but the results missed our quality bar. Completing the task wasn't enough.

Try one local page: ask Copilot to submit an empty form and report the error it actually sees. Review its evidence. Start with test data and limited permissions.

The move: from asking for code to checking a workflow.

GitHub Copilot browser use: a seven-slide first-test checklist.

WHAT CHANGED
GitHub announced browser use in public preview on November 17, paired with its Chrome extension.

WHAT IT DOES
Copilot can interact with web apps, help debug them and automate browser tests. Preview access and your client's setup still matter.

WHY BUILDERS CARE
You can move from requesting a page to inspecting a real interaction. Our latest Tech Thursday image experiment proved the distinction: the CLI produced a batch, but the host still had to judge its quality.

TRY THIS THIS WEEK
Use a local form and test data. Install the official Chrome extension and enable browser use in your supported Copilot client. Confirm the connection. Ask: "Submit this form empty. Report the validation you observe. Do not change the app or submit real data."

Write your expected error first. Compare it with the observed result. Keep permissions limited, and review any proposed fix before accepting it.

THE SIGNAL
AI isn't just drafting an answer. It's entering the workflow. Your acceptance criteria are what make the result useful.

Save this for your first browser-use test.
